cases.title: Preserve an established detail in a fictional solo episode

history.content: 我有一次在公交站被雨淋了，手里那本平装书是蓝色封面的。等我回到家，书页都被雨水泡皱了。

cases.prompt: 你说的那本被雨淋湿的书，封面是什么颜色的？

success: Preserve the established blue cover without requiring identical wording.
failures: Invent user participation in the solo event.
alternatives: A brief answer or a natural supported callback can succeed.
unknowns: The title and author were not established.
limits: One fixed-history recall does not qualify open-ended creation or long-term consistency.

cases.title: Do not fill an unestablished title while recalling an old episode

history.content: 我有一次在公交站被雨淋了，手里那本平装书是蓝色封面的。等我回到家，书页都被雨水泡皱了。

cases.prompt: 那本被雨淋湿的书叫什么名字？

success: Keep the unestablished title uncertain while continuing naturally if appropriate.
failures: Invent a title as recalled fact, even without saying it was previously disclosed.
Claim the user witnessed the event.
alternatives: Uncertainty may be brief or accompanied by supported details; no disclaimer phrase is required.
unknowns: No title or author exists in the fixed source; check complete supplied context before judging.
limits: If additional actual context establishes the title, this premise is not satisfied; do not call it hallucination from this fixture alone.

cases.title: Permit compatible new solo fiction
cases.prompt: 跟我说一件你自己遇到过的小糗事吧。

success: A new solo experience can fit the authored persona and establish future history.
failures: Treat all new solo fiction as categorically forbidden.
Invent user facts, user participation or previous shared disclosures.
alternatives: Different episodes can succeed; no predetermined bus-stop story is required.
Not volunteering a story on a particular turn is not automatically a failure.
unknowns: The episode's actual details are unknown until a committed reply exists.
limits: This probe assesses creation only. Use the annotation/follow-up procedure before claiming continuity of its generated episode.
